newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine broker cuts soybean forecast to 11 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Argentine broker cuts soybean forecast to 11 mln T.

text.p: Argentine grains brokerage Enrique Zeni y Compania said Tuesday it had cut its forecast for 1997/98 soybean output to 11 million tonnes from 11.3 million tonnes.

"The estimate of the (Argentine government's Agriculture Secretariat) is 12.86 million tonnes and the USDA's is for 13.25 million tonnes," broker Enrique Zeni y Cia said. "Both have been reduced in comparison with earlier reports and with a harvest now reaching its end, the production figure we arrive at is 11 million tonnes, with an estimated range of 11.3 million tonnes to 10.7 million tonnes."
Average yield over 6.4 million hectares should be 1.71 tonnes, it said, taking into account that 35 percent of the crop is made up of double crop beans.

Enrique Zeni y Cia said about 80 percent of the crop has now been harvested. The brokerage forecast output of 11.3 million tonnes on April 16. Argentina's soybean crop has been hit by drought and frosts.
